articles.headline: NBA Finals: Wemby's Jackals bring European fandom to Spurs-Knicks
articles.description: Handpicked by Wembanyama, the Spurs' 83-member fan club turns Section 114 into a roaring, choreographed spectacle.

images.name: Jackals [608x342]
images.caption: Behind the vision of Victor Wembanyama, the Jackals, the Spurs "ultras" supporters, call Section 114 their home.

images.name: Jackals 2 [608x342]
images.caption: Much like European soccer supporters, the Jackals have come up with their own chants with original lyrics set to familiar songs.
images.credit: Photos by David Dow/NBAE via Getty Images

images.caption: How the Jackals came to be a presence at Spurs games

articles.headline: Trump accepts invite to attend NBA Finals Game 3 in New York
articles.description: President Trump said Thursday that he has accepted an invitation from New York Knicks owner James Dolan to attend an NBA Finals game at Madison Square Garden next week.

images.name: Donald Trump [600x400]
images.caption: Donald Trump attends Sunday's game between the Commanders and Lions. Only two other times did a president go to an NFL game during the regular season while in office, according to the league: Richard Nixon in 1969 and Jimmy Carter in 1978.

articles.headline: Sources: NBA eyes interaction between Jalen Brunson, fans in Game 1
articles.description: The NBA is investigating an interaction between Knicks star Jalen Brunson and courtside fans late in the fourth quarter of Game 1 of the NBA Finals, sources confirmed to ESPN.

images.caption: Jalen Brunson was visibly frustrated over an interaction with a courtside fan during a pair of conversations with official Scott Foster in Game 1 of the NBA Finals.

articles.headline: NBA championship and Finals MVP odds: Knicks, Brunson new favorites
articles.description: The New York Knicks are now the championship favorites after their come-from-behind road victory over San Antonio in Game 1.

images.name: Jalen Brunson [1296x729]
images.caption: Jalen Brunson led all scorers with 30 points in an impressive Game 1 win over the Spurs.
images.alt: Jalen Brunson #11 of the New York Knicks dribbles the ball during the game against the San Antonio Spurs during Game One of the 2026 NBA Finals on June 3, 2026 at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas.
images.credit: Nathaniel S. Butler/NBAE via Getty Images

images.name: Victor Wembanyama [1296x729]
images.caption: Victor Wembanyama (center left) and the San Antonio Spurs are favored entering the NBA Finals.
images.credit: Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images

images.name: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander [1296x729]
images.caption: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Victor Wembanyama are Nos. 1 and 2 in the Finals MVP odds, respectively.

images.name: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander [608x342]
images.caption: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and the Thunder are back to being odds-on title favorites after taking a 3-2 series lead over the Spurs.
images.alt: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander

images.name: Jalen Brunson [608x342]
images.caption: Jalen Brunson has the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals for the first time since 1999.
images.alt: Jalen Brunson

images.name: Knicks/Cavs [1296x729]
images.caption: The Knicks are looking to end the series against the Cavaliers tonight, as they have the second-shortest title odds and are an overwhelming favorite to win the East.
images.alt: New York Knicks guard Landry Shamet (L) defends Cleveland Cavaliers guard Donovan Mitchell (R) during game 3 of the NBA East Conference Finals between the Cleveland Cavaliers and the New York Knicks in Cleveland, Ohio, USA, 23 May 2026.

images.name: Jalen Brunson [608x342]
images.caption: The Knicks are now heavy favorites to win the Eastern Conference after taking a 3-0 series lead over the Cavs.
images.alt: Jalen Brunson
images.credit: Nathaniel S. Butler/NBAE via Getty Images

images.name: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander  [1296x729]
images.caption: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander how has even odds to win the Finals MVP.
images.alt: Oklahoma City Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (2) takes a shot as San Antonio Spurs guard Stephon Castle (5) defends during the first quarter during game two of the western conference finals for the 2026 NBA playoffs at Paycom Center.

images.name: Victor Wembanyama, Jalen Williams [608x342] - Copy
images.caption: VIctor Wembanyama poured in 41 points and grabbed 24 boards in the Spurs' thrilling Game 1 win.
images.alt: VIctor Wembanyama

images.name: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander [1296x729]
images.caption: The Thunder enter the Western Conference Finals as the odds-on favorite to win the NBA championship.
images.alt: Oklahoma City Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (2) looks for an outlet against San Antonio Spurs guard Stephon Castle (5) during the first half of an NBA basketball game, Tuesday, Jan. 13, 2026, in Oklahoma City.

images.caption: Cade Cunningham and the Pistons are favored heading into Game 7.

images.name: De'Aaron Fox [1296x729]
images.caption: The Spurs took care of business with a big Game 5 win at home against the Timberwolves.
images.alt: De'Aaron Fox #4 & Dylan Harper #2 of the San Antonio Spurs high five during the game against the Minnesota Timberwolves during Round Two Game One of the 2026 NBA Playoffs on May 4, 2026 at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas.

images.name: Jalen Brunson [1296x729]
images.caption: The Knicks advanced Sunday with another blowout victory over the 76ers.
images.alt: Jalen Brunson #11 of the New York Knicks celebrates during the game against the Philadelphia 76ers during Round Two Game Four of the 2026 NBA Playoffs on May 10, 2026 at the Wells Fargo Center in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.
images.credit: Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images

images.caption: LeBron James and the Lakers are big underdogs against the defending champion Thunder, and Game 1 only lengthened their odds.

images.caption: The Knicks have surged to +850 to win the NBA Finals following the first-round exit by the Boston Celtics.

images.caption: Even after pulling out the win over the Lakers on Wednesday night, the Rockets remain big long shots to win the NBA championship.

article.story: NEW ORLEANS -- — Ryan Rollins made a career-high seven 3-pointers and scored 27 points to help the Milwaukee Bucks beat the New Orleans Pelicans 139-118 on Friday night for their third straight victory and sixth in seven games. Playing without injured star Giannis Antetokounmpo, the Bucks pulled away in the fourth quarter to improve to 24-30. Antetokounmpo has been sidelined four weeks by a strained right calf. Bucks newcomer Cam Thomas, a former LSU star, had 27 points in 21 minutes off the bench, and Kevin Porter added 25 points. Rollins was 7 of 10 on 3s and had six assists, four steals and two blocks. The Bucks were coming off a victory at defending champion Oklahoma City before the All-Star break. Zion Williamson led New Orleans with 32 points in the first game of home back-to-back, while scoring leader Trey Murphy sat out because of a sore right shoulder. The Pelicans dropped to 15-42. Rollins had 16 points in the first half to help Milwaukee take a 71-65 lead. Williamson had 21 points in the half. The Bucks took a 103-96 advantage into the fourth. After the Pelicans cut it to 108-102 on Williamson’s layup, the Bucks pulled away with a 14-4 run. Pete Nance hit two 3s and a layup during the run. Up next Bucks: Host Toronto on Sunday. Pelicans: Host Philadelphia on Saturday night. ------ AP NBA: https://apnews.com/hub/nba
